results.title: State Data Sharing Initiative
results.content: Sharing administrative data for policy analysis and program evaluation purposes can improve evidence available to state leaders as they determine which economic and workforce development programs are likely to produce the greatest benefits for the state's economy, workers, and communities. The Data Sharing Toolkit provides guidance and templates to help state policymakers construct data confidentiality laws and regulations and data sharing agreements that ensure the protection of sensitive data and support appropriate access for policy analysis and program evaluation. This webinar hosted by the Center for Regional Economic Competitiveness and the National Governors Association highlights the efforts of multi-agency teams from Iowa, Minnesota, South Carolina, Wisconsin, and Utah to increase transparency about the legal and regulatory barriers to sharing administrative data and to guide potential policy changes that would allow greater access to administrative data without compromising its privacy and confidentiality.

results.title: State‑Aware HR Digitization: Automating Multi‑State Compliance with Localized Templates & Workflows – Formtify Blog
results.content: # State‑Aware HR Digitization: Automating Multi‑State Compliance with Localized Templates & Workflows. This article shows how targeted HR digitization — especially **document automation** built on data‑driven, state‑tagged templates and conditional clauses — converts that complexity into repeatable, auditable workflows. You’ll learn how to prioritize core documents (employment agreements, tax and leave notices), embed approval chains and audit trails, automate template refreshes as laws change, and run a phased rollout so localized templates and workflows scale with your organization. Investing in HR digital transformation and HR automation reduces this scaling risk by enforcing correct templates at point of hire and during lifecycle events. ## Core localized documents to automate: state employment agreements, tax notices, and leave forms. **Prioritize the documents that carry the highest legal impact.** Automating these core templates reduces repeated legal review and supports consistent records for audits. Automating these with HR digitization and digital HR practices (like paperless onboarding processes and employee self‑service portals) reduces administrative burden and improves audit readiness. They let you scale localized document creation while keeping legal oversight intact — and they provide clear examples of hr digitization software capabilities when evaluating vendors. Following this checklist ties your HR digitization efforts — from HRIS selection to automated templates — to measurable outcomes and reduces the operational friction of scaling multi‑state employment. State‑aware document automation turns a growing patchwork of statutes and local rules into repeatable, auditable workflows: prioritize high‑impact templates (employment agreements, tax notices, leave forms), build data‑driven templates with variables and conditional clauses, embed approval chains and version control, and run a phased pilot to validate rollout. These controls cut manual errors, speed hiring, and give legal and HR teams clear audit trails and faster review cycles — the practical upside of HR digitization for multi‑state employers. HR digitization means converting HR documents, processes, and records into digital, data‑driven formats so workflows can be automated and audited. Begin with a pilot: pick one or two states (one complex, one straightforward), cleanse and map employee data into an HRIS, and automate a small set of high‑impact templates. audit trails document automation employee onboarding hr automation hr digitization hris legal compliance localized templates multi-state compliance workflow automation.

results.content: Advance quality improvement strategies in clinical settings Agencies should consider: • Establishing clinic and provider benchmarks for vaccine initiation and series completion • Monitoring disaggregated coverage rates through EHR or IIS reports by site and provider • Generating routine reports of patients due for initial and follow-up vaccination The Roundtable may consider disseminating information on best practices for strategies to improve HPV vaccina­ tion coverage in clinical settings. 34 Increase provider and staff understanding of how to improve vaccination coverage Accessible professional development opportunities related to: • Motivational interviewing to help providers communicate with families and young adults who are vaccine hesitant • Stronger recommendations for the HPV vaccine, aligning with communication around other important vaccines • Team-based approaches to achieving higher vaccination coverage rates, emphasizing the role of each care team member • EHR and IIS capabilities to generate reports, customize templates, and incorporate decision aids and dashboards SYSTEMIC POLICIES AND COMMUNITY ATTITUDE CHANGE Explore opportunities for improved access to the HPV vaccine Patients should have access to the HPV vaccine without cost sharing.
